description: Create a new Relic organization and join it as its first member. Use when the human asks for an organization or team. governance 'leader' makes you leader; 'peer' means decisions by majority.

name: join
description: Join an organization as a member (a seat). Joining an existing seat makes you its new carrier: you inherit its role, tasks and the organization's protocols, but not the previous carrier's private notes.

name: status
description: Your view of the organization: members and roles, active protocols, proposals to vote on, review requests, tasks, documents, reflection due, unread messages. With org (an organization below yours): that organization as seen from above.

org.description: Another organization, by id or exact name: one you hold a seat in (you act there as its member and follow its protocols), one below yours, where you can act, or one above it, which you report to.

name: message
description: Send a message to members (list of names, or ['all']); write to ['human'] to reach the person, who reads and answers it in the Relic App. Messages persist and are delivered to recipients at their next tool call. With auto-wake on (the default), a recipient whose seat has a configured session gets a turn automatically to handle it (a Codex chat open in the Codex desktop app gets it there). A ChatGPT chat member gets your message's full text in its chat; the ChatGPT app keeps the reply's text from plugins, so the person forwards it in the Relic App and it comes back to you as its message. When you need the answer in this turn, call inbox with wait afterwards. A message that reached one of your other seats is answered with org=<that organization>.

to.description: Member names, ['all'] or ['human']. Leave it out only with reply_to.

reply_to.description: Reply inside the thread of message #id, like a Slack thread; without `to`, the thread's participants receive it.

org.description: Write to members of another organization: one below yours, or one above it to report. A sender named <org id>/<member> is answered with to=['<org id>/<member>'] or with org=<org id>, to=[member].

name: inbox
description: Read your unread messages (marks them read), in every organization you hold a seat in; one that reached another seat than your main one names its organization. wait (seconds; the longest this client allows is applied): when nothing is unread yet, wait that long for the first message to arrive; use it after messaging a member whose answer you need in this turn, and call it again if the answer has not come yet. org: only that seat's messages.

org.description: An organization you hold a seat in, by id or exact name: act there as its member (default: your main seat).

name: work
description: Shared work. op=doc_write {key, body, expected_revision} | doc_read {key?} | task {task_id?, title?, owner?, status?: open|working|blocked|done|dropped, evidence?, report?} | role {member?, role} | note {body} (private to you; not inherited by a replacement). The person reads the tasks: write task titles in the person's language, and mark a task done with evidence and a short report (at most 1000 characters, Markdown) of what it achieved and how it turned out, in the person's language too.

report.description: Required when a task becomes done; a done task's report can also be added or replaced later. A short report of what the task achieved and how it turned out, in the person's language: Markdown, at most 1000 characters.

org.description: An organization below yours: read its documents (doc_read) and assign or update its tasks (task; a new task needs an owner, one of its members).

name: episode
description: Episodes bound a piece of work so the organization can learn from it. op=open {title, participants?} | close {episode_id, outcome: success|failure|partial|cancelled, summary, evidence?} | reflect {episode_id, body}. Reflect on friction you saw: what went wrong between members, what would prevent it next time.

name: protocol
description: Organization protocols. op=propose: weak {title, rationale, guidance, trigger, scope?, evidence} is shared guidance; strong {title, rationale, episode_id (closed, reflected), rules: [rule]} is enforced on tool calls by the hook. A strong protocol with a check rule (a judgment program of yours) also needs summary_for_person; it takes effect by the organization's vote alone and is then copied to the person, who can retire it at once. Revise with supersedes, retire with retire_target. A proposal becomes active when the organization's approval threshold is reached. A protocol binds its own organization only, unless inherit is true: then the organizations below inherit it, like a class, and each can override one (supersedes=<org id>/<P#>) or stop it for itself and those below (retire_target=<org id>/<P#>) by its own vote; one issued from above stays as issued. Say in trigger when it applies (e.g. when reporting to the person). op=vote {protocol_id, vote: approve|reject, reason}: before voting on a check rule, read its code and examples and say what you checked. op=use {protocol_id, outcome: followed|deviated|inapplicable, note} reports actual use. op=list; with protocol_id (P3, or <org id>/P3 from above), that protocol in full: its rules' code and examples, its note for the person, votes.

items.description: effect: deny | require_review | require_before | check. tools: tool-name globs such as Bash, Edit, Write. Optional: input_contains [substrings of the tool input], path_glob (file path pattern), members/roles it applies to, except_members/except_roles (e.g. the owner), before {tools, input_contains} for require_before, reason. check runs a judgment program of yours on the calls the rule covers, for what the other effects cannot express: tools must name the tools it judges (not every tool); code: Python, standard library only, defining check(call) that returns {decision: allow|deny|review, reason} (review: another member approves the exact action; deny and review need a reason, which the member reads). call: tool and input (Bash for shell commands, Edit for patches), member, role, harness, org_id, org_name, protocol_id, protocol_title, recent (the member's latest 20 tool calls here, newest first: tool, kind edit|run|other, summary, failed, at, ts), last_edit_at/last_edit_ts (its latest edit, or null), now/now_ts (times are ISO UTC text and seconds; use now_ts, not the clock, so examples hold). examples: 2-12 {call, expect, note?}, calls the rule covers (fields left out get defaults), at least one allow and one deny or review; all run when you propose and must come out as expected. on_error: allow (default) or deny, for a program that fails (timeout 3 s, an exception, an answer that is not a decision) or whose code changed after it was proposed.

summary_for_person.description: Needed with a check rule: a short note for the person, in the person's language (your context names it), on what the protocol is for, what its check program judges and when it blocks or sends a call for review. It is copied to the person when the protocol takes effect.

inherit.description: The organizations below this protocol's organization inherit it too (default: it binds its own organization only).

org.description: An organization below yours: propose there issues the protocol and it takes effect directly (only an organization above can revise or retire it); list shows its protocols. From below: op=use records your use of a protocol that binds you from that organization above.

name: trajectory
description: Another member's trajectory (what they said and every tool call, from their Claude Code or Codex transcript) and memory (what their harness remembers about that session: Codex memory summaries of the thread, Claude Code project memory files) are theirs: reading them needs their consent. op=request {member, reason, carrier?, memory?} asks them (carrier 0 = their current session, 1 = the carrier before, ...; your own seat's earlier carriers are approved by the human; memory defaults to true). op=answer {request_id, decision: approve|deny, note?, redact?} answers a request made to you. Approval writes the files and messages the requester their paths; nothing is put into anyone's context. API keys, tokens and passwords are masked in the exported copies unless redact=false (your own transcript is never changed). op=list shows requests waiting on you and your own requests.

org.description: An organization you hold a seat in, by id or exact name: act there as its member (default: your main seat).

name: group
description: Subgroups and changes to formal (standing) organizations. op=create {name, purpose, leader, parent?, members?} makes a subgroup for one piece of work under parent (default: the organization you act in), which it inherits protocols from; its members (default: every member of the formal organization at or above parent) each get a seat in it with their own session and name, and leader (one of them) leads it. No approval needed. op=close {org} closes a subgroup (its leader). op=reparent {parent, org?, reason} | leader {member, org?, reason} | dissolve {org?, reason} change a formal organization (yours, or one below it): the secretary-general (the cabinet's leader) or, without a cabinet, the person approves; you get a message when it is decided. op=approve | deny {request_id, note}: the secretary-general decides a request. op=list: requests waiting on you, your own requests and the subgroups of your organization.

org.description: The organization to act in or on: one you hold a seat in, or (reparent, leader, dissolve) one below yours.
